deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a laboratory notebook entry from Gauss's magnetometer work (Göttingen, early 1830s; magnet bars from the instrument maker Rumpf, a mirror on a brass rod, a wooden bar). The page contains no mathematics beyond instrument arithmetic.

(1) Table of oscillation times. These are the times of oscillation (seconds) of the four middle bars A, B, C, D, swinging with the wooden bar and mirror, copied from the previous page and taken before and after successive magnetization by stroking:
- A: 28.52 → 26.74 (60 strokes) → 25.31 (60 more) → 24.76 (more).
- B: 27.96 → 24.18 → 25.07.
- C: 21.00 after stroking with A and B.
- D: 25.99 → 23.86 (120 strokes).
The moment of inertia I is essentially unchanged, and T = pi*sqrt(I/(M*H)). So the magnetic moment satisfies M ∝ 1/T^2, and a shorter period means a stronger magnet.
- For B the period rose again from 24.18 to 25.07 after further stroking. Gauss notes: 'the cause of the decrease of intensity at B remains uncertain'. The loss is (24.18/25.07)^2 ≈ 0.930, i.e. about 7%.
- For A the total gain is (28.52/24.76)^2 ≈ 1.327.
- For D the gain is (25.99/23.86)^2 ≈ 1.187.

(2) Calibration of the mirror's correction screw.
- 9 1/8 whole threads span 3.7 mm. One thread is therefore p = 3.7/9.125 = 0.4055 ≈ 0.405 mm.
- The screw acts at radius r = 56 mm. One turn tilts the mirror by p/r = 0.405/56 = 0.0072321 rad. Multiplying by 206265″ per radian gives ≈ 1491.7″ = 24′51.7″ ≈ 24′52″, as Gauss writes.
- In scale units, one turn is now 55.5 divisions (56.15 is written above as an alternative/earlier value).
- Implied value of one division: 1491.7/55.5 ≈ 26.9″. The next page gives 80.5″/2.95 ≈ 27.3″, which is consistent.

(3) Collimation (mirror normal vs. magnetic axis) adjustment by reversal. The magnet with mirror is read in two reversed positions (labelled West/East).
- West 309.52, East 209.75; difference 99.77 divisions (written −99.77 as East − West).
- If the mirror normal makes an error e with the magnetic axis, reversal changes the reading by 2e. So one screw turn changes the West−East difference by about 2·55.5 = 111 divisions.
- The full correction needed is 99.77/111 ≈ 0.90 thread [my inference]. Gauss applies 3/4 thread, predicting a change of 83.25. He observes West 269.5, East 250.9, difference 18.6, an actual change of 81.2, in good agreement.
- He records that the rear end stands 173.7 mm from the centre of gravity.
- A further 1/6 thread (predicted change 18.5) gives West 257.2, East 253.9, difference 3.3 (actual change 15.3).
- The means of the two positions (259.6, 260.2, 255.55) drift only slowly, reflecting the variation in declination.

(4) The page ends by noting that a very large correction was also made in the sense of the short diameter of the mirror. The next page continues with the final collimation error of ±2.95 divisions = ±80.5″.

The whole page is an experimental-physics protocol: magnetization of bars and adjustment of the mirror magnetometer by the reversal method.
errors: No arithmetic errors. 3.7/9.125 = 0.4055 is correctly rounded to 0.405, and 0.405/56 rad ≈ 24′51.7″ is correctly given as 24′52″.

The first correction (3/4 thread) is deliberately smaller than the ≈0.9 thread implied by the reversal theory. The second (1/6 thread) produced slightly less effect than predicted (15.3 vs 18.5 divisions); this is within the observational and declination-drift noise, not a mistake.

results.what: Magnetic intensity of bars inferred from oscillation periods before and after stroking (M proportional to 1/T^2)
results.modern_name: Oscillation (Gauss) method for magnetic moment / intensity

results.what: Angular value of one thread of the mirror correction screw: pitch/radius = 0.405/56 rad ≈ 24′52″ ≈ 55.5 scale divisions
results.modern_name: Screw/lever calibration of the mirror-and-scale (optical lever) reading

results.what: Elimination of collimation error between mirror normal and magnetic axis by reversing the magnet and adjusting the screw by half the difference
results.usually_credited_to: Standard astronomical/geodetic instrument practice; applied to magnetometers by Gauss

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine laboratory notes of Gauss's well-documented magnetometer work: bar magnetization, screw calibration and reversal adjustment. They are useful as a working record but contain nothing mathematically new.

checkable.asserts: 9 1/8 threads spanning 3.7 mm give a pitch of about 0.405 mm
A pitch of 0.405 mm acting at radius 56 mm tilts the mirror by about 24′52″
The observed change after 3/4 thread (81.17) differs from the predicted 2*55.5*0.75 = 83.25 by only about -2
Intensity ratio of bar B after/before the last stroking (24.18 → 25.07 s) is ≈0.93, a decrease
Intensity gain of bar D after 120 strokes is ≈1.187

transcription_corrections: The machine transcription's 'Umwendung' is consistent with the image ('eine Umwendung', i.e. one turn); this reading is correct.
Last value under A reads 24.76 on this page (the previous page has 24,70); the image supports 24.76.
'betragen 18¾ 9⅛ ganze Gewinde 3mm7': 18¾ appears to be an earlier/struck figure, and the operative value is 9⅛ threads = 3.7 mm (consistent with 0.405 mm per thread).
The headword above the readings is 'Scalentheile', and the 56.15 above 55.5 is an interlinear alternative.
The marginal words read 'also unsere oben / unten', apparently referring to mirror orientation.
